title: On-call Simulation Cookbook and Ops Rotation Guidelines
author: Aisha Patel
body:
Summary

This document is a compact but actionable cookbook for on-call rotations, structured game days, simulated incidents, and customer-facing status communications. It consolidates the practical runbooks and templates most commonly used during incidents at Redwood Inference, focusing on deterministic decision points, minimal viable comms, and reproducible simulation exercises to keep on-call muscle memory sharp.

Scope

- Audience: SREs, Platform Engineers, Serving Runtime owners, and any engineer in the on-call rotation.
- This doc covers: rotation policy, handoffs, triage playbooks for common failure modes, game-day exercises with learning objectives, postmortem and RCA template, and status page + customer comms templates.

Roles and responsibilities

1. Primary on-call (Pager): first responder for alerts, owns initial triage and mitigation, runs runbook steps or escalates.
2. Secondary on-call (Bridge Lead): covers ongoing incidents when primary needs help; manages the incident bridge and coordinates cross-team actions.
3. Incident Commander (IC): appointed for Sev2/Sev1 incidents after initial triage; responsible for overall mitigation strategy and customer comms.
4. Service Owner: owner of the affected service or model; responsible for post-incident remediation and follow-up.
5. Eng SRE Manager: approves postmortem severity and escalation of change freezes or rollbacks.

Incident lifecycle (simplified)

1) Detect: Alert fires, PagerDuty page to primary.
2) Triage (0-10 minutes): Primary acknowledges, collects 1-line symptom, impact, scope.
3) Mitigate (10-60 minutes): Apply runbook mitigations, enable fallbacks if needed.
4) Stabilize (60-180 minutes): Confirm system recovery or apply longer-running remediations.
5) Restore and Communicate: Update status page and customers.
6) Postmortem: Owner writes report within 72 hours, action items tracked to completion.

Triage checklist (first 10 minutes)

- Acknowledge and read the alert message.
- Identify affected service and region.
- Scope: number of customers impacted, internal-only, or global.
- Severity decision: use Redwood severity definitions (Sev1 = customer-visible outage with major impact; Sev2 = degraded but usable; Sev3 = minor).
- Immediately open a Slack incident channel and start a Zoom if cross-team coordination needed.
- Add initial note to status page draft (template below).

Quick decision matrix

- If > 10% of requests or any paid customer blocked -> escalate to Sev1 and notify IC.
- If latency increased but no functional errors -> Sev2.
- If single-host OOM affecting one worker pool -> Sev3 unless cascading.

Runbook excerpts (examples)

A) High tail latency for text-generation endpoints

1. Confirm via metrics dashboard: 95th and 99th latency graphs, CPU and GPU utilization, and KV cache hit rate.
2. Check recent deploys: review rollout status in Redwood Console (check canary failures).
3. If GPU saturation: scale up worker pool if autoscale is available, or redirect traffic to a lower-latency compatible model.
   - CLI example: redwoodctl scale --pool model-serving-east-1 --replicas +2
4. If KV cache degraded: restart caching service on affected hosts, monitor rewarming.
5. If rollback required: follow controlled rollback steps in deployment ADR.
6. Update incident channel and status page every 30 minutes until stable.

B) Model-serving process OOMs on a host cluster

1. Identify offending host(s) and taint them from the pool: kube cordon + drain.
2. Retrieve crash logs: journalctl -u model-serving or run the runtime crash inspect script.
3. Temporarily route traffic away from the pool and restart a small number of workers to validate.
4. If crash reproduces on stable model version, escalate to Runtime team and collect heap dumps and model config.

C) Control plane unresponsiveness (API 5xx for console or admin APIs)

1. Verify whether user-facing inference endpoints are impacted; separate customer-facing comms if not impacted.
2. Restart control plane pods in order: leader first or follow documented restart order.
3. If database connectivity errors present, failover to read replica and open an incident to DBA and infra teams.

Escalation matrix

- Primary -> Secondary after 20 minutes if mitigation not progressing.
- Secondary -> IC for cross-team coordination or customer-impacting incidents.
- IC -> CTO or Head of SRE for Sev1 major incidents or if > 2 hours unresolved without meaningful progress.

On-call rotation policy (practical rules)

- Rotation length: 7 days for SREs and Platform engineers.
- Handoffs: mandatory written handoff message in Slack and update the oncall-handoffs channel. Handoff checklist includes current incidents, outstanding action items, and expected busy windows.
- Blockers: members can swap shifts up to 48 hours before the start; urgent swaps must be approved by the oncall manager.
- Escalation contact list: maintained in the oncall roster doc and updated monthly.

Handoff message template (Slack)

- Date/time of handoff.
- Current active incidents and status lines.
- Items to watch overnight (e.g., model retrain job, capacity scaling window).
- Any maintenance windows.

Game day syllabus (quarterly)

Goal: simulate realistic incidents to validate runbooks, tooling, and human processes. Organize exercises against three axis: technical, communications, and postmortem quality.

Sample exercises:
- Exercise A: Regional GPU fleet outage. Objective: validate routing and model fallbacks.
- Exercise B: Regression in a model variant causing high error rate. Objective: practice rollback and canary analysis.
- Exercise C: Synthetic DDoS on the control plane API. Objective: capacity throttling and status page updates.

Game day logistics:
- Duration: 3 hours per session with 30 minutes of dry run, 2 hours scenario, 30 minutes debrief.
- Roles: facilitator, observer/scorekeeper, IC, primary responders.
- Success metrics: mean time to first mitigation, quality of status updates, and completeness of postmortem draft within 72 hours.

Postmortem and RCA template (required within 72 hours)

- Title and Sev level
- Incident timeline (timestamps in UTC)
- Impact statement: customers affected, cost, and business impact
- Root cause analysis: bullet points and evidence links to logs, traces, and deploy history
- Corrective actions: owner, due date, verification steps
- Preventative items: design changes or runbook additions
- Blameless summary and learnings

Status page and customer communication templates

Initial notification (first 15 minutes)

- Short subject: Redwood Inference API: Degraded Performance in region X
- Body: We are investigating elevated latency for the Redwood Inference text-generation API in region X. Customers may see increased latency or occasional errors. We will provide updates every 30 minutes. Affected customers: all requests routed to region X. Impact: increased tail latency, possible 5xx errors. Mitigation steps in progress: scaling worker pools and assessing recent deploys. Next update in 30 minutes.

Follow-up update (example)

- Subject: Update: Incident ongoing, mitigation in progress
- Body: The team has identified GPU saturation on a subset of hosts and has added capacity to the pool. Error rate has decreased from 4% to 1.2% over the last 20 minutes. We are monitoring. Estimated time to resolution: 1 hour.

Resolved notification

- Subject: Resolved: Service restored in region X
- Body: The issue causing elevated latency has been mitigated. All customer traffic is serving normally. We will publish a postmortem within 72 hours. If you still see degraded performance, contact support.

Status page API example (curl)

- Draft an update locally and post via status API

```
curl -X POST https://status.redwood.ai/api/v1/incidents \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $STATUS_TOKEN' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"summary":"Elevated latency in region X","status":"investigating","components":["text-generation-east-1"]}'
```

Live docs and tooling references

- PagerDuty playbook: link in oncall tooling page.
- Incident channel names: #inc-<shortid>-<service>.
- Runbook repo: internal git with versioned runbooks and playbook tests.

Metrics and SLOs to watch during incidents

- 95th and 99th latency per model (target 95th < 300ms for small context workloads).
- Error rate (5xx) threshold: alert when > 0.5% sustained for 5 minutes.
- KV cache hit rate: alert when < 60% for a serving pool.

After-incident follow up

- Postmortem owner publishes draft within 72 hours.
- Action items get JIRA tickets with owners and due dates.
- Verification: owner must post verification evidence when item is complete.

Appendix: quick reference table

- Alert: high-99th-latency -> Runbook: latency playbook -> Owner: runtime-team -> Escalate to: IC after 20 min
- Alert: control-plane-5xx -> Runbook: control plane restart -> Owner: platform-infra -> Escalate: DB team if persistence errors

Contact and maintenance

- Oncall roster link: internal directory (updated monthly).
- Emergency contacts: Eng SRE manager and CTO.

Revision history

- 2025-02-14: Updated to clarify handoff process and add status API snippet
